Meta announced today the launch of several new devices equipped with AI features, including the palm-sized Muse Charm device, designed specifically for its new AI assistant Muse. Details are as follows.

Meta expands its AI smart glasses product line

Meta held its annual Meta Connect 2026 conference today, showcasing its latest achievements in artificial intelligence technology, wearable devices, and VR products.

Last year's most talked-about new product was the Meta Ray-Ban Display, the company's first smart glasses with a built-in display that can show messages, navigation, and Meta AI interactive responses.

At the time, Meta's AI smart glasses had already received a considerable market response, with Meta and EssilorLuxottica selling more than 7 million pairs combined throughout the year.

However, since then, Meta glasses equipped with cameras have been controversial in terms of privacy and ethics, with extensive discussions across society on privacy, ethics, and broader backlash against AI.

Meta launched its first smart glasses without a camera today—the Ray-Ban Meta Audio—priced from US$349 and going on sale on October 13.

The Ray-Ban Meta Audio retains features such as music and podcast playback, calls, and real-time translation, offering the same rich audio experience as the camera-equipped version, and supports Meta's recently launched personal AI assistant Muse.

In addition, Meta also unveiled the Ray-Ban Meta (3rd generation) tonight, featuring a slimmer design, up to 9 hours of battery life, and a new shortcut button, while retaining the 12-megapixel camera and 3K video recording capabilities introduced in the previous generation.

Users can customise the function of the new button within the Meta AI app to launch Meta AI or other features—such as real-time translation—with a single press. The Ray-Ban Meta (3rd generation) goes on sale today, priced from US$449.

At tonight's event, Meta also unveiled the Meta VR Glasses, a VR headset weighing only about 100 grams that looks more like ordinary glasses. The device features what Meta calls a "5K infinite display built with micro-OLED panels," has built-in Meta AI, supports eye and hand tracking, and relies on a small pocket-sized base for computing, power, and storage.

Meta positions the VR Glasses as a personal cinema, esports device, and workspace, emphasising that this is the first VR device to receive IMAX Enhanced certification, supporting 3D films and immersive live sporting events.

Alongside the Meta VR Glasses, Meta also launched new holographic features that can generate realistic virtual avatars reflecting the user's real-time expressions and reactions during video calls.

Meta stated that some of these features will be introduced to the Meta Ray-Ban Display in the future, allowing users to create digital faces for hands-free video calls, with WhatsApp being the first supported application.

The Meta VR Glasses will go on sale in spring 2027, priced at US$1,299.99.

To summarise tonight's glasses product news, Meta also expanded its Meta Glasses product line, adding two new designs—Capri and Nova—as well as the latest collection designed in collaboration with LISA, and launched the Meta Adventurer at US$249, the most affordable smart glasses to date.

The company also simultaneously launched a limited-edition Meta Fury style, as well as a new Ivory colourway in collaboration with Kylie Jenner.

Meta unveils Muse Charm

At tonight's event, Meta also announced the Muse Charm—a palm-sized device tailored for its recently launched personal AI assistant Muse. Meta officially launched the Muse application earlier this month, which promptly topped the charts on the US App Store and Google Play.

According to Bloomberg, the Muse Charm was developed by Meta's newly established design lab, led by former Apple interface design chief Alan Dye, in collaboration with the company's Superintelligence AI team.

Meta describes the Muse Charm as a "holdable device," equipped with an approximately 2-inch OLED touchscreen and featuring a customisable Muse character at the centre of the interface. Users can change its appearance, clothing, voice, and other attributes, and interact directly with Muse through the device.

The device also has built-in front and rear cameras, speakers, microphones, 5G connectivity, and a USB-C port. The cameras can be used to take photos and videos, but Bloomberg noted that their primary purpose is to provide visual information for Muse to conduct analysis and AI-assisted operations, rather than serving as a traditional camera.

Users can set up and sync through the Muse app on iPhone or Android. When two Charm devices are brought close together, they can also recognise and interact with each other.

Meta plans to officially launch the Muse Charm in December. The company has not yet announced pricing, but Bloomberg expects its price to be comparable to that of a smartwatch.
